input:
The isolation for the calibration check is carried out with the unit stopped and the standby pump in service. The check takes about 86 min with the unit isolated, and the isolation must be proved before the instrument is disturbed. The order of the steps follows the order of the isolation itself: duty is transferred first, the machine is isolated second, and the isolated section is proved safe before any joint is broken.

The duty pump is stopped at the local panel and the run-down confirmed on the panel indication. The standby pump is then started, and discharge pressure must be confirmed as held by the running machine before any valve is moved; the standby pump carries the duty for the whole check, and no isolation step is taken until the changeover is complete and stable. The duty pump suction isolation valve is then closed, followed by the discharge isolation valve, and the locks and tags are fitted under the PTW. The padlock keys remain with the holder who fitted them.

Stored pressure remains in the casing and in the suction line even after the valves have been closed. The isolated section is drained and vented to the closed drain, and is treated as live until the vent runs clear and the local gauge reads zero. The isolation is proved at the gauge and again at the drain point before any joint is broken; a section that will not depressurise is reported to the shift supervisor and left locked, rather than forced.

Once isolation has been proved, the calibration check proceeds on the isolated instrument, free of flow and free of pressure. The 86 min covers the isolation, the check itself and the reinstatement. Reinstatement reverses the order of isolation: the section is refilled and vented, locks and tags are removed by the holder who fitted them, and the valves are reopened in the order given in the changeover procedure. The duty pump returns to service only when the instrument is back in circuit and reading, and the standby pump is stood down in the normal changeover once the duty pump is carrying the load again. If a check cannot be completed as written, it ends with the unit left isolated, the PTW still open, and the instrument state recorded in the shift log.
